citation.authors: Oyake K, Murayama J, Tateishi T, Mochida A, Matsumoto M, Tsujikawa M, et al.
citation.title: Comparison of the sit-up test and head-up tilt test for assessing blood pressure and hemodynamic responses in healthy young individuals

population.description: Nineteen healthy adult volunteers analysed (21 recruited, 2 lost to technical failure of the haemodynamic measurement); nine male, the rest not split by sex in the paper (mixed). Age 24.3 ± 2.4 years and BMI 20.9 ± 1.8 kg/m2 as printed in Results; the ± is not labelled SD or SEM anywhere, so no sd is entered. Inclusion: aged 20 to 40, no underlying disease, no history of syncope; 'healthy' is the paper's word.

protocols.name: supine_rest
protocols.description: Supine rest on a motorized tilt table for 10 min before either test (sit-up, or 70-degree head-up tilt; order randomised, 10 min apart; each Table 1 supine column pools both orders, so about half of each column's supine rests followed the other test and the first-in-session rest cannot be separated; the two columns are the same 19 people in the same state, so only the sit-up column is entered). Minute 0 is the start of the 10-min rest; the supine value is the mean of its final 2 min (minutes 8 to 9, window 8 to 10), per Methods. Fed state: the paper says only that participants refrained from eating and caffeinated products for at least 2 h before each test, so no meal is entered and the arm starts from typical values (norm_center). The tests were run between 18:00 and 19:00 (printed as 'between 6:00 and 7:00 p.m.'); 18.5 is the middle of that hour. The second test's supine rest came after the first test's upright period and the 10-min rest between tests, which the arm does not carry. No derived input: no meal, dose or intensity.
